ai.description: This 40–50 mm frog has a lime-green dorsum with scattered black spots. It features a distinct white sub-tympanic line and translucent, pale-yellow webbing on the feet.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Polypedates zed* is best distinguished from similar species by its unique, distinctively patterned, reddish-brown reticulations on the hidden surfaces of its thighs.
ai.habitat: The Narayanghat Whipping Frog inhabits subtropical moist broadleaf forests and riparian zones, typically found at low to moderate elevations across the Indian subcontinent.
ai.behavior: The Narayanghat whipping frog is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for insects among vegetation near water bodies.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Polypedates zed* breeds during the monsoon, laying eggs in foam nests attached to vegetation overhanging water. Each clutch typically contains 100–200 eggs.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Polypedates zed* is endemic to the Terai region of Nepal, specifically found in the Chitwan District near Narayanghat at low elevations.
ai.callDescription: The Narayanghat whipping frog produces a series of short, high-pitched "tink" or "click" notes, typically heard from vegetation near stagnant water bodies or marshes.
